Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

REFERENCE NOTES — Mara and Luis Ortega’s family photo archive

Mara Ortega and her brother Luis are assembling photographs from three branches of their family in a small archive at their mother Elena’s house in Tacoma. The collection is not a public gallery. It is meant to help relatives find images, understand who and where they show, and make a dependable local copy before Elena’s basement is renovated. Luis has scanned most of the prints from their father’s side; Mara has phone pictures and albums from their mother’s side. Their cousin Nina contributed several folders from reunions and school events. The oldest identified photograph is a studio portrait of Elena’s grandmother, dated in pencil to 1912, although nobody has yet confirmed the date.

The current working directory is on a desktop computer in Elena’s sewing room. Mara created folders by year when a date was known, but scans with uncertain dates are in a folder called “needs a second look.” Luis added some descriptions in a spreadsheet, including names, event locations, and who supplied each image. Several filenames still come directly from scanners, such as IMG_0048, so the family does not want a setup process to assume every filename is meaningful. They have not agreed on a single naming convention. Elena wants to be able to browse the archive without having to learn a complicated application, and Luis prefers not to move the original scans until there is a verified copy.

Mara wrote in the planning email, “If we can find the reunion pictures without asking three people, I’ll call this a success.” Elena said, “I mostly want to know which box a picture came from, even if we never learn the date.” Nina’s reply was, “Please don’t make my school photos searchable by everyone with the link.” The family has not decided whether Nina’s concern applies only to her school folders or to all images she contributed. They want the setup helper to keep those remarks in view while distinguishing confirmed settings from questions that still need an answer.

There are two storage devices on hand. Elena’s desktop has a 2 TB internal drive with about 640 GB free. Luis brought a 4 TB external drive, which is currently labeled “Ortega spare” and contains an older copy of family videos. He says those videos are also important and must not be erased to make room for photos. The family has not checked how much space the video folders use or whether the drive has errors. The external drive can be connected during visits, but Luis takes it home afterward. Elena’s computer is usually on during the day and is shut down overnight.

The following settings were drafted after Mara read the archive software’s local-storage page. The family wants the helper to explain how this block fits into a proposed setup, without silently changing its values:

[local_archive]
retain_days = 24
allow_remote = false
name = "local-copy"

A remote-sharing feature is available in the software, but nobody has enabled it. Mara thinks it might make it easier for cousins in other states to view selected reunion pictures. Nina is worried that a shared link could be forwarded. Luis said, “Let’s get the local copy right before we talk about links.” Elena does not use the software yet, and the family has not chosen who would be allowed to invite relatives if sharing is considered later. Any explanation should keep local storage and possible remote access distinct rather than treating one as a decision about the other.

1. Questions the family has already raised
   - Which folders should be included in the first import: only the dated folders, or also “needs a second look” and the scanner-named files?
   - Can the spreadsheet descriptions be attached to images without changing the scan files themselves?
   - How can the helper verify that the existing videos on Luis’s external drive remain untouched?
   - Should the family make a second copy on another device before any cleanup or reorganization?
   - What information does Elena need for simple browsing, and what should remain visible only to the people organizing the archive?

These are questions, not approved requirements or answers. Luis can check the external drive’s available capacity next time he visits, but no date has been set. Mara can bring the spreadsheet and a sample of uncertain-date scans; Elena has asked that the helper not rename files during the first discussion. The family has not chosen a backup schedule, decided whether to buy another drive, or agreed on a person responsible for checking copies. They also do not know whether the archive software can preserve spreadsheet fields exactly, so that capability should be checked rather than assumed.

At the last kitchen-table meeting, Mara demonstrated three examples: a 1988 summer picnic with a handwritten place name on the back, a group portrait from an undated reunion, and a set of digital pictures sent by Nina after a school concert. The picnic’s location is spelled two different ways in the spreadsheet. Elena recognized two people in the reunion portrait but was unsure of one name. Nina’s concert images include other students, and she has not said whether those families agreed to wider sharing. The group agreed that descriptions should show uncertainty where it exists instead of turning guesses into facts.

The next visit is penciled in for the first Saturday in May, but Luis may arrive later because of work. If the external drive is not connected during that visit, the family can still discuss the folder structure and review sample images; they cannot verify a copy on that drive then. Mara expects to bring a laptop with the spreadsheet, while Elena will have the desktop available. There is no scheduled migration or deadline.
